correctness.rationale: The directed one-outdegree sandpile translates binary firing supports exactly. The terminal vertex link has precisely the triangle and edge given in the proof and is a cone, furnishing five elementary collapses per trailing zero. The base complex consists of one tetrahedron, one triangle and a path; four+one+one+one elementary collapses yield a cycle on L=g+2 vertices. This gives an unrestricted integral simple-homotopy proof with exactly \(7+5t\) collapse pairs. The embedded verifier independently simulates 156 cases, checks 5,772 free-face pairs, and computes 42 mod-two homology cases. Finite checks support but are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The closest original primary study treats one consecutive block, a three-grain separated support, or a single missing grain, but it neither states nor implies that two separated adjacent pairs collapse in exactly \(7+5t\) elementary pairs for all gaps and trailing-zero lengths. The explicit uniform dominated-vertex elimination and arbitrarily large first-Betti drop after adding a grain are additional structural conclusions. Targeted phrase, alias, parameter, homotopy, and record searches found no dominating prior statement; this is evidence of novelty, not proof of historical uniqueness.

value.rationale: The paper establishes rich topology and variable Betti numbers in binary path avalanche complexes. Two separated length-two blocks form a minimal natural extension of its separated three-grain family. The new all-parameter collapse determines integral homotopy and shows an arbitrarily large first-Betti reduction from t+2 to one after adding exactly one grain, including an explicit constant-size polygon core independent of trailing length. This is a substantive stability and sensitivity phenomenon, not merely an isolated small computation.
